stimulus:
A church bell is tuned after it is cast, not before. The founder pours bronze
into a loam mould built around a core shaped by a strickle board, lets it cool for
days, and then mounts the bell upside down on a vertical lathe. Metal is shaved from
the inside of the bell in thin rings, and each cut lowers particular partials: the
hum, the prime, the tierce, the quint, the nominal. Shave too much and the bell
cannot be put back; the only remedy is to melt it down and start again.

Before you start, here is a piece of unrelated material. You may let it inspire your thinking in any way you like, or not.

<material>
A church bell is tuned after it is cast, not before. The founder pours bronze

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with AP-1 degron, then re-challenge
ideas.description: Expose cells to a defined transient stimulus (e.g., TNF, wounding, or growth factor pulse), then acutely deplete AP-1 (FOS/JUN family) with a degron at different times after the stimulus. Re-challenge weeks later and measure whether the primed transcriptional response persists without AP-1 present, separating AP-1 as a maintainer from AP-1 as an initiator.

ideas.title: Longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN of AP-1 occupancy and accessibility
ideas.description: Profile chromatin accessibility, AP-1 motif footprints, JUN/FOS binding, and H3K27ac/H3K4me1 at time points from during stimulus to many cell divisions after it is removed. Test whether AP-1-bound enhancers stay open or become 'latent' after stimulus, and whether AP-1 binding is required to keep them so.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome lineage tracing of memory inheritance
ideas.description: Combine single-cell RNA/ATAC with clonal barcodes or live-cell reporters to compare memory states in sister cells and across divisions. If AP-1-dependent states are heritable, sister cells should show correlated accessibility and re-activation kinetics beyond what is expected from shared environment.

ideas.title: Locus-specific perturbation with dCas9 tools
ideas.description: Use dCas9-based recruitment or blocking of AP-1 motifs, plus CRISPR deletion/mutation of specific motifs at candidate memory enhancers. Check whether altering a single AP-1 site abolishes or creates memory at that gene (faster re-induction, retained accessibility) in cis, independent of global AP-1 levels.

ideas.title: Dose, duration, and composition sweeps with live reporters and modeling
ideas.description: Vary the strength, duration, and frequency of stimuli and AP-1 dimer composition (e.g., FOS vs. JUNB vs. ATF3 overexpression) while tracking AP-1 activity and target gene reporters live. Fit mathematical models (hysteresis, bistability, positive feedback) to test whether AP-1 dynamics show the signatures of a self-sustaining memory circuit versus a purely transient signal-following response.
